Encore 0.3.0: no more terminal setup. Encore now installs what it needs to
play music by itself, after asking you once.

## Download

| System | File |
|---|---|
| macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) | `Encore_0.3.0_universal.dmg` |
| Windows 10 and 11 | `Encore_0.3.0_x64-setup.exe` (or the `.msi`) |
| Debian 12+, Ubuntu 22.04+ | `Encore_0.3.0_amd64.deb` |
| Other Linux (glibc 2.35+) | `Encore_0.3.0_amd64.AppImage` |

You no longer need Python, Node.js, Deno or Bun installed.

## First launch

These builds are not code-signed yet.

- **macOS:** open the app once, then go to **System Settings → Privacy &
  Security** and choose **Open Anyway**. macOS asks once for access to your
  saved session in the Keychain.
- **Windows:** SmartScreen warns on first run. Choose **More info**, then
  **Run anyway**. If Smart App Control is on, Windows blocks the app.

Then Encore offers to **set up playback**. Choose **Install**: it downloads
65 to 80 MB into its own folder (120 to 160 MB on disk) and shows each step
as it goes. You can keep browsing meanwhile.

## What's new

- **No more terminal setup.** Encore downloads the components it plays
  music with (yt-dlp, and the Python and Deno it runs on) into its own
  folder, with your OK. Nothing else on your computer changes, and no admin
  rights are needed.
- Every download comes from the projects' official releases over HTTPS and
  is checked against a checksum built into Encore before it is used.
- If you choose **Not now**, pressing play brings the setup back instead of
  skipping songs, and the song starts as soon as setup ends.
- Setup recovers from a lost connection, a full disk, a cancelled or
  interrupted download, or quitting halfway: **Try again** picks up cleanly.
- When a newer Encore uses newer components, including yt-dlp, it updates
  them on launch without asking again, with a small notice. The current ones
  keep working until the new ones are ready.
- **Settings → Playback** shows the components and their versions, and can
  reinstall them or remove them to free the space.
- The Debian package no longer depends on `python3`, `python3-venv` or
  `nodejs`, and the AppImage works on systems without Python.

## Fixes

- **Linux:** Encore now runs on Ubuntu 22.04 and Debian 12; earlier builds
  wouldn't start there. It no longer crashes at launch on systems without a
  D-Bus session (it runs without media keys instead).
- A damaged library database no longer makes Encore close at every launch:
  it's set aside and a fresh one is made. If Encore can't start properly, the
  window now says why and where the log is, instead of disappearing.
- When nothing can play (no internet, YouTube asking for a bot check, or
  playback not set up), Encore says so once instead of skipping through your
  queue. Songs that can't play explain why in plain words: age-restricted,
  not available in your country, Premium-only, private or removed.
- Messages stay up long enough to read, look like errors when they are, and
  show even with reduced motion turned on in Windows.
- Audio recovers when the output device is disabled and re-enabled, or stops
  responding, and the player bar says when there's no audio output.
- A loading spinner shows while a song gets ready, and skipping quickly
  through songs no longer prepares every one of them.
- Pages that failed while offline load again by themselves when the
  connection returns.
- The player bar and side panel show proper empty states on a fresh install.
- On macOS, opening Encore twice brings back the running one instead of
  starting a second copy, and denying Keychain access explains itself.
- Importing a browser session that turns out to be signed out keeps your
  previous session instead of leaving you stuck on "Choose a channel".
- Windows: paths with non-English characters (such as `C:\Users\José`) work,
  and the first window fits small screens without hiding behind the taskbar.

The old yt-dlp environment from earlier versions is deleted once the new
components are in place.

Encore is unofficial and not affiliated with YouTube or Google.
